human_tolerance.notes: Seemingly unfazed by considerable human activity: it hunts from utility poles and motorway verges, nests in urban parks, and one bird raised young in Manhattan. It perches over a garden rather than foraging in one.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Prenesting courtship in late winter or early spring, when copulation can occur numerous times each day and lasts 5 to 10 seconds; a pair may hold the same territory for years.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The pair builds a stick nest of twigs lined with bark, pine needles, corn cobs and stalks, 71 to 97 cm across, in a large tree or on a man-made structure; one to three eggs are laid, and fledging, including learning to fly and hunt, takes some 10 weeks.

vocalizations.description: A long, harsh, descending screech. The hawk calls frequently while hunting or soaring, and loudest in annoyance or anger, in response to a predator or to a rival hawk's intrusion into its territory.
A wailing klee-uk food cry uttered by young hawks when their parents leave the nest.

range.note: Country list reduced from the article's range description: breeds across Canada and the continental United States, and has established populations in Mexico and Puerto Rico. The Central and South American wintering grounds are left off rather than guessed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'Often, they scan for prey activity from an elevated perch site, swooping down from the perch to seize the prey', 'When soaring or flapping its wings, it typically travels from 32 to 64 km/h, but when diving, may exceed 190 km/h', and the falconer note that it 'allows it to perch in a tree or other high vantage point' cover perching, powered flight, soaring and the short walk to seized prey.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The pair constructs a stick nest in a high tree', 'The nest is generally 71 to 97 cm in diameter', built 'of twigs lined with bark, pine needles, corn cobs, husks, stalks, aspen catkins, or other plant lining matter', or on a man-made structure or a cliff ledge.

traits.perching.note: 'It may be used as perch sites' and 'shorter primaries result in wingtips that don't reach the tail in perched birds'; it is a perch hunter by definition.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of 'typically weighing from 690 to 1,600 g'. The article also notes that a multi-site study found males averaging 837 g and females 1,040 g, close to this midpoint.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of 'a wingspan from 110-145 cm'. The article's later figures for the wingspan, 105 to 141 cm, give a near-identical midpoint.

traits.lifespan_y.note: The article says only that red-tailed hawks 'are also long-lived and highly disease-resistant, allowing a falconer to maintain a red-tailed hawk as a hunting companion for many years', and gives no figure. 12 years is a deliberate low-precision estimate for a large accipitrid of this longevity class and is approximate, not a sourced value.

traits.diet.note: 'Prey varies with regional and seasonal availability, but usually centers on rodents, comprising up to 85% of a hawk's diet', with birds, fish, reptiles and amphibians taken opportunistically; 'Hawks will eat carrion if need be, although it is not a preferred food source.'

traits.social.note: 'The same nesting territory may be defended by the pair for years' and 'Red-tailed hawks, like some other raptors, have been observed to hunt in pairs'; outside the breeding season birds hunt alone.

traits.activity_pattern.note: The bird is described as scanning from a perch, soaring and diving in daylight, and its call is tied to annoyance at a rival or a predator; diurnal activity follows directly.

traits.defense.note: The described response to a threat is to vocalize loudly in annoyance or anger, to the predator or to a rival intruder; the species is not described as attacking people.

traits.wariness.note: 'Unlike some other raptors, the red-tailed hawk is seemingly unfazed by considerable human activity and can nest and live in close proximity to large numbers of humans', including the Manhattan nesting pair.

habitat.use.note: 'Its preferred habitat is mixed forest and field, with high bluffs or trees that may be used as perch sites' and 'The construction of highways with utility poles alongside treeless medians provided perfect habitat for perch-hunting'; the split between time on a perch and time on the wing is a judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: It hunts and roosts from an elevated perch - a tree, a bluff or a utility pole; 'perch' is the matching drawable shelter tag.

habitat.resources.note: Rodent-dominated predation, scavenging when needed, a large stick nest in a tree or on a structure, and elevated perches; weights are judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Utility poles along highways, urban parks and a successful Manhattan nest are all described explicitly.

seasonal.strategy.note: The article describes a bird that holds a territory year-round and never describes a migration; year-round residence with juvenile dispersal is the honest reading, though no explicit statement of residency is made.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Follows from the year-round territorial behaviour described: the pair is on the same ground in winter.

seasonal.phases.note: 'In the same period, the pair constructs a stick nest', with 'prenesting courtship in late winter or early spring' and 'fledging, including learning to fly and hunt, takes some 10 weeks'; the calendar windows here are a judgement placed on those statements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'a clutch of one to three eggs is laid' and 'fledging, including learning to fly and hunt, takes some 10 weeks'; 70 days is that sourced 10 weeks and the 0.7 scale is a judgement.

vocalizations.screech.note: 'The red-tailed hawk frequently vocalizes while hunting or soaring, but vocalizes loudest in annoyance or anger, in response to a predator or a rival hawk's intrusion into their territory.' The harsh descending quality of the call is standard description of the species and is authored here rather than quoted.

vocalizations.klee_uk.note: 'Young hawks may utter a wailing klee-uk food cry when parents leave the nest.'

look.note: Dark brown upperparts with a pale chest and a darker belly band, hooked bill and yellow legs, and the brick-red tail the species is named for; palette, proportions and box placement are judgement, with the red carried on the tail part so the name reads in the model.

behavior.note: The shared fsm-seabird-predator-v1 program is reused even though its name says seabird: its states (patrol on the wing, hunt tagged small_vertebrate, scavenge carrion, flee by flight, rest at shelter) are a red-tailed hawk's year-round behaviour almost item for item. flee_m and calm_m are raised well above the defaults because the bird is 'seemingly unfazed by considerable human activity', so a person at the default 12 m would trigger a permanent flee state that the species would never actually show.
